Kowloon walled city was demolished in the 90s. Which was of course for the best, a place that densely packed was a massive fire hazard waiting to happen, and with all the buildings being connected, a fire in one apartment would have spread to the others very easily while evacuations would have probably been a nightmare if not impossible (panicked people rushing out all at once might have clogged the stairwells and exits), but at the same time, it's also a shame. It was just such  a unique social and architectural phenomenon, I almost wish they hadn't demolished it and instead turned it into a giant museum people could tour.

The Walled City of Kowloon was actually once a military fortress that became derelict.  Impoverished HK'ers slowly filled it up over the course of 40 years, as real estate space on the tiny island kept shrinking and the population kept growing.  The Walled City had its own schools, shops, pharmacies, barbers, etc all wound together by tiny crooked overlapping passageways.  It's said that many people who lived within the Walled City of Kowloon never saw the true light of day.

I'm glad that you take the time to criticize the game, while also acknowledging that full studio games can also give off the same sort of feeling. That back-and-forth feeling can be unavoidable sometimes, and as a story writer, it can be hard to write a cohesive story that feels new and refreshing around every turn. Sometimes you have to go back to an area multiple times, and it can be hard to make it feel "not so same-y." But I'm glad that you acknowledge a well-known game that can also give off those kinds of vibes. I think a lot of people nowadays think that, if a game is published by a big studio, it MUST be good and polished, but if it's an indie game, they expect bugs and worse writing than the big studios can offer, and that's not always the case. Your horror gameplay is what I started watching you for, and I'm glad you give indie games the spotlight they deserve

"Fatal error. Out of memory. Vivarium halted."

"I have more questions!" he screams.

"Fatal error. Out of memory. Vivarium halted."

Manic hyperventilating gives way to calmer gasps. Finally, the survivor places a hand on the bio bed, and breathes, "Goodbye, Sophie."

We remember the joy they brought into ordinary days.
We remember the way they made people smile without even trying.
We remember the stories, the jokes, the questions, the hugs, the little moments that now feel more precious than gold.

May we honour them not only with tears, but with tenderness.
May we speak their names with love.
May we carry their memory with care.
May we hold one another a little closer because they taught us, even in heartbreak, how precious love truly is.

Though their lives were brief, their light was real.
Though their journey ended too soon, their memory will walk with us always.
And though we release them today with broken hearts, we entrust them to peace, to love, and to the arms of eternity.

You were loved beyond measure.
You will be missed beyond words.

It’s actually impressive how some people will watch this and still find a way to blame the stalking victim for her stalker. No guys, she didn’t lead him on. He was her neighbor who had probably wormed his way into her life, and in a moment of compassion, she called to make sure he was okay. She was probably calling everyone she knew to make sure they were safe. I know for damn sure that’s what I would do if a bomb went off in my area. Also he was the one that pressured her into letting him come over. She NEVER asked him to come over.

I actually love the way the game dev handles the narrative. Even when you’re playing through the POV of the obsessive character, his actions still don’t seem normal in the slightest. When he’s hurting himself at the end and she’s crying, it’s *very* clear that she isn’t crying because she’s ‘seen the error of her ways’ or ‘finally understands what he means to her’ 

She’s crying because she’s witnessing something graphic and disturbing. She wants no part of this and he’s the one forcing her into this situation.

I do think there’s a larger metaphor at play and that can definitely be down to interpretation -and yet this game still manages to make the overall experience very clear. So kudos to the game dev!!! ❤️

OK here's a few things I think I can clear up about this game's lore 

(Spoiler Warning)





3:47: Regarding the climber we play as; we still have no idea their origin, or if they even have worked at the superstructure. It's widely assumed that we are an outsider, primarily due to how often Habitation Yellow's SAPS announcements label our presence as an "unidentified human" or an "intruder." However, logs confirm that something disabled all the safety protocols, so it's possible we may have worked here, and the security is just... hostile.

10:54: Regarding the Substructure Automated Processing System being "alive," it most likely is not. For the April Fools event, the voice actor (Holly) had fun recording little tidbits like this, which were not meant to be taken seriously. In the main game, there have yet to be instances of SAPS showing sentience beyond certain anomalous circumstances (such as the Delta 45 artifact and the Ladder anomaly).

14:30: Yup, that is not the surface. The ITAA dug under the Ruby Mountains to find the structures you climb in, meaning everything (even the surface of the Abyss) is underground. This also explains why SAPS calls it the "Superstructure Cavity." We do not know what the surface's fate even is, and if it's even habitable anymore.

19:40: Regarding the face, and if it replaces the goop or not, yes and no. The face is the replacement for the goop during the Abyss levels, but the face is ALSO the goop, just mutated to continue to chase us horizontally across the Abyss, like a toxic ex with attachment issues. As of this comment, we are unsure if it will stay the face following the next regional update, or revert back to its goopy ways (or potentially not be present at all).

It couldve easily been like "ooooh, the mountain is actually a METAPHOR!  OOOO!  It's aggrandizing time!"  But instead approaches it more like "yeah, obviously the mountain is a metaphor.  No need to dwell on it too hard, because i assume you got that."  Its really mature and the balance between complexity in your writing, respecting the audience's intelligence, and refraning from being overly indulgent is like satan's triangle for writing.

Thai resident here, here's some more info about the snacks: 
-  หมูหยอง (pork floss) is typically sweet, fluffy, and slightly savory; “Na Lon” in the name "ข้าวตังหน้าล้น" (Khao Tang Na Lon) literally means “overloaded topping”.  
- The milk tablets are essentially compressed powdered milk, a nostalgic childhood snack. The most famous brand is Suan Dusit, initiated by the late King, and also weirdly popular with Chinese tourists (no-one knows why)
- Cory Fin - yes, cough drops, excellent purchase 
- Tamarind (มะขาม - ma-kaam) is a fundamental flavor in Thai cuisine. Mark's expressions capture the taste well; it has an initial sharp sourness, but is usually mixed with salt or spice and becomes balanced after a while,(Thais love combining sweet, sour, salty, and spicy)
- The gummy bears and "dipping sauce" are inspired by a very common Thai snack called มะม่วงน้ำปลาหวาน (ma-muang-naam-blaa-waan) which is sour mango dipped the sweet fish sauce as seen. To a foreign tongue, its an insane flavour profile at first, but trust me it's fantastic. 
- Bonus Fact: The modern Thai alphabet mimics the Latin (English) alphabet, mainly influenced by Western sans-serif fonts to make it easier to read. So the "WS" you see on many of the products is actually ฟรี  (Phonetically pronounced f-r-ee, and, as you may have guessed, literally means "free"). Other common letters are ส ('s' sound but when written looks like an 'a')

The thing is, viruses mutate, adapt, evolve. Elpis might be a counter to the current G, T, Orborous and other virus-based B.O.W.s and weapons developed from the Progenitor Virus, but it isn't a counter to the fungal Megamycete or the Las Plagas parasites.

There's no guarantee that the B.S.A.A., which has been corrupted from within by the Connections before, won't leak the Elpis 'cure' to outsiders, who might try to salvage the bio-terrorism market with Elpis-resistant B.O.W.s. Or that the viral weapons might not develop a resistance in the same way that modern viruses developed a resistance to current antibiotics due to over-use and concentration in the hospital systems that resulted in 'the super-bug'.

Elpis is a good story concept to trim down all the world-ending super-weapons back to a handful of things and not eighty bajillion things that the writers have to juggle all at once.

The T-virus (& G) was created from the progenitor virus they found in a flower in Africa, which was its natural host (see RE5).

Also viruses and mold (a fungus) are completely different lifeforms; viruses are arguable not even alive, just genetic material in a shell.

Just got to watch Iron Lung today (it was released late here in India). What a film man!! Such an amazing true to genre 
I love slow burns in general (social media reels didn't ruin me yet), so i enjoyed the heck out of this. The tension, the build up, the acting, the dialogues, everything created such a dark and gore atmosphere it was right up my alley I felt. 

Tho sometimes I did find it difficult to watch as it was soo dark i couldn't see what was happening (don't know if it's my theatre's fault or not, someone can correct me here), I was still able to have fun and was at the edge of my seat all the time. Last 30 mins was just me realising mark's love to his craft. 
Bringing David Szymanski's vision to the big screen is not easy because it's hard to keep the audience hooked the whole time and I understand when people say it's not everyone's cup of tea. 

The amount of character's lore this man has dropped throughout the film, the slow dripping of water, the importance of shield, the constant clicking of pictures, everything was soo thought out and intentional. 

Overall, a solid 8/10 and definitely one of the best psychological horror movies for me.

I think I figured out something I didn't know needed figuring out. The reason Nate wants the privacy of a bathroom is the same reason he didn't want to go home and he's always in his room and the same reason he wears a damn full body pajama getup. He's ashamed of himself. He doesn't want anyone to see him.

Knowing that Bennet Foddy likes putting philosophy into his games even the rage inducing ones, I had a feeling there’d be some lesson or some topic to think about in this one. It didn’t really come together for me just what Nate’s actions through the game meant until the wish scene.

He’s an adult living with his parents, not making anything of his life. He’s socially awkward, he doesn’t live up to his parents expectations or his sisters success, and he refuses to ask for help despite needing it until it’s literally forced upon him (like the lantern). He doesn’t stick up for himself, and has a hard time getting through anything on his own. It feels jarring for the sudden depth to be dropped here, but it’s been built up to this point. You can see how he interacts in this world, you can just imagine how it is in the real world. You’re getting a glimpse into what his problems are throughout the game as goofy and bizarre as it is. It’s pretty well done. Very existential and a little depressing, with a lot of humor to balance that out.

The collective (throttle and rotor pitch controls) are better suited center line of the helicopter, which puts that in your left hand while you can control the cyclic (forward, aft, left, right) or joystick with your right. There's definitely a lot of elements of the female experience that lend to the horror aspect here, more than any traditional mode of horror. Mike has zero boundaries despite Sydney being outwardly negative towards his advances, but she also still values him as a friend and doesn't want to lose him like that. She obviously trusts him enough to sleep in the same house as him, but it started to feel towards the end that he would have been willing to assault her and that's terrifying in itself. And then you add in being alone in a house where a random person has access to you (and has demonstrated that they will use that access without your consent, even when threatened) that isn't who they say they are, another random person who *stalked you* from a restaurant because you didn't give them a ride- notice he is antagonistic towards her, but not towards Mike, who owns the fucking truck-and it boils down to just another day as a feminine person where you don't know if you're safe. Every male character Sydney interacts with, besides the pizza workers I guess, is unsafe. Nora is the only other woman that says more than a sentence. 

Anyways I agree with the sentiment that as a fifth installment there's more of an expectation for immersion, and I think some of the elements of horror may have been lost because of that, but the story itself is a different kind of scary than a typical "ghost in the house" or "monster chasing me" type horror. Mark has a really good point at the end about these Spot The Difference games; it IS something many of us did as an activity as kiddos. I think one of the reasons this vector of gameplay works so well is because the ability to notice small changes in your enviroment is one of those Survival Skills that gets brain to make with ALL the happy juice when we practice them ( see also long distance hiking, DIY water purifcation, and caring for plantlife; all things our ancestors had to do to live well ). It pairs well with horror because the ability to notice small changes is self same with the ability to notice a jaguar hiding in the brush that wasn't there the last time you looked. Adrenaline kicks, demanding action. With the big cat, the action demanded is BOOKIN IT or trying to scare the predator off. Adrenaline is particularly good at getting hoomans past the freeze that occurs when Fight Or Flight must be selected, forcing a decision to break a deadly impasse. If the correct decision was made, That Person Lives, their brain goes I SURVIVED!!! YAAAAAAA and all those happy hormones cements the memory in place as Important To Remember And Share. 

In spot the difference games, you also have an impasse that must be resolved; report or continue. If you make the right choice, you Took Action and the same mechanism rewards that action while becoming more invested in the progress towards escape. It is a simulation that hits SO WELL and rewards behaviors that we already want to practice. 

Hmmmmm... now I wonder what other types of childhood play can translate to gaming, and what mechanics they'd pair best with...

Okay so for anyone wondering there are multiple ends. There’s 5 in total. 

1. Coming Home to Roost
The standard ending. 

2. Fox Wedding
Unlocked by not taking red capsules, purifying the sacred sword, and obtaining the Agura no Hotei-sama. In this ending Hinako accepts the pre-ordained marriage to the fox guy. 

3. The Fox Wets Its Tail
Unlocked by not taking red capsules and obtaining the unpurified sacred sword. In this ending she chooses freedom from the fox guy and shu. She’ll also confront the fox god and choose her own path. 

4. Ebisugaoka in Silence
Unlocked by not taking red capsules, purifying the sacred sword, and meeting certain requirements after obtaining at least two other endings. In this ending Hinako rejects both Shu's control and the arranged marriage with the Fox guy. 

5. The Great Invasion from Space! (UFO)
A secret, joke ending that is unlocked by listening to all UFO radio broadcasts, finding all three "The Great Space Invasion" movie posters, and then finding the movie review after fulfilling the other conditions. 

The difference between ending 3 and 4. In ending 3, "The Fox Wets Its Tail" is the "good" ending where human Hinako rejects her fate and escapes with Shu, but the fox god's influence is lost, causing the town to become uninhabitable. In ending 4, "Ebisugaoka in Silence" is the true canon ending where human and fox Hinako reconcile.

I have sound and photo sensitive epilepsy. This movie was the first time I have been to a theater since I was 8 years old. I worked for weeks to make sure I would be able to see it safely. Meds, headphones, earplugs if i needed them, a blanket, my loving wife beside me, and over a year of nervous system regulation therapy. 

I watched the movie. It was the best movie I have ever seen. Genuinely. I didn't know what theaters were like. The way the floor shook with the base, how massive the screen was. The sound the lights it was all so intense. 

This movie was such a massive accomplishment, for mark, for the community, for indi film making. For me, it was proof that if I took care of myself, accomidated myself, I could do things again. I could leave my house. Be in a loud theater watching a horror movie with every seizure trigger under the sun blaring at me. 

I didn't seize. I was safe the whole movie. It was so intense. It felt like living for the first time in a long time. And I know a massive part of it was having this symbol of safety that has been carved into me since childhood standing at the helm, living through every bloody moment in this immersive masterpiece with me. 

I am getting better. And doing things. And living again. And I got to watch Iron Lung. Isn't that cool?

FYI, Mark's upset about webcam placement is basically just an aspect of mise en scene, which refers to the placement of things within a scene, essentially. In cultures where you read left to right, placing something on the right and having it look or move from right to left is used in film to make something feel off or disconcerting. Having something on the left and looking towards or moving towards the right, by contrast, is a natural and logical progression. Having something in the far left and facing the left or right and facing right can make things feel awkward and claustrophobic. You typically want some head space and open space in the direction that the subject is looking while framing a shot, per the study of mise en scene, unless you are trying to incite a particular emotional reaction from the audience. This is essentially the "mise en scene for dummies" version, but it's an interesting study focus of film production.

Went to see Iron Lung and loved it. Not just as a Markiplier production or a game remake or even an indie movie, but genuinely as a standalone movie in its own right. Honestly, not really knowing if it would be my thing, I took a chance on it just because I've seen such good direction and acting with WKM, HWM, ISWM, Wilford Motherloving Warfstache, etc, and it didn't disappoint. 

I genuinely loved the slow suspense and psychological horror (more so than the action scenes) and the writing and acting was refreshingly good because it wasn't afraid to be real, show the genuine emotional and physical grind that too many movies these days skip in favour of instant action. Sure, there were a few things that didn't hit the mark for me personally, but I'd expect that from most good films anyway. Overall though, a movie that can hold my attention purely based on good acting, character and relatability is fantastic. Truly awesome - and even the occasional dry humour laugh (the 'password' scene had me laughing for too long - subtle, easy to miss, hilarious).

Plus, being someone who suffers with social anxiety, going to the theatre alone was a big step - yet somehow I felt compelled enough to push through that to support a very talented creator. 🤟So thank you- and here's hoping for more awesome projects in the future.

For anyone who wonders, here is a brief story breakdown 

(spoilers ahead)










1: The members of The Ward, the original colony set up by prism to research the canal, fall victim to an unknown infection found in the canal (the weird mushroom things)
2: The entities 1 and 2 appear, either from the canal as well or as mutated humans who fell victim to the infection. Entity 02 (female, possible 01's mother) dies by choking on an apple from the tree (Adam and Eve)
3: years later, a new colony is set up on the moon that is The Plaza. 
4: During a routine patrol after a quake, the original infected Ward member is discovered by John, he is infected and returns to infect the others
5: the AI discovers the infection, locks down communications, and tasks the 05 droids with killing all living inhabitants to contain the infection
6: A software Engineer (you) who was sent for before the communications lockdown shows up and is placed in isolation. Either already infected or infected early into the game

From there over the course of the game we shut down the AI and unlock the canal to facilitate the spread of the infection. All the rest of this is more theories, but the infection, some sort of hive mind, is the one giving us the tasks we "see" in our terminal. The exact dates or identities of the monsters are unknown. The infection (likely the voice at the end) appears to be adding humans to itself so they may "endure" rebirthing them as a part of its design. Likely fated to become more entities as the infection perfects its evolution of humanity.

Then from 71% to 72%, it took 1:07 seconds, an 8 second increase, 14% of 59 is 8.26, those were the last three numbers we saw. I wrote a longer theory under part 8 about Silent Hill F being less about “leaving childhood behind” and more about the loss of self and the specific horrors tied to womanhood, identity, and being shaped by others. After watching this part, I just wanted to add a few more things that really stood out to me.

During Hinako’s identity crisis, after the doll (a symbol of her innocence, past, and sense of self) reminds her of her name, she starts asking herself if she really is Shimizu Hinako. The fox-masked man appears to comfort her, but when he “reassures” her, he doesn’t use her full name. He tells her she is his Hinako. He removes her family name entirely, like he wants her identity to stop being tied to her past or her family and exist only in relation to him.

That also made me think about her sister. Hinako mentions she hasn’t seen her since she was married off, and when she finally appears, she’s “different.” Her face is replaced with a bird mask. It’s not a fox mask like the other women’s. To Hinako, her sister is still her own person, but her face (her identity) has been overwritten to match her husband.

And then there’s Hinako returning to her childhood home after (what I assume is) marrying the fox-masked man. She comments on how everything feels wrong. Her home doesn’t feel like home anymore. It’s full of strangers (the monsters), reminders of what her life used to be, and proof that this fate was always closing in on her. Her memories of pushing back, of fearing she’d become like her mother (submissive and trapped in an abusive relationship) all come rushing back.

Like I said in my earlier comment, I’m only seeing this through Mark’s playthroughs, but these moments really feel like they’re reinforcing that central theme: womanhood in this story isn’t just about growing up. It’s about how easily identity can be erased, rewritten, or handed over to someone else. I really hope these memories (and her saving Shu) are the cracks that finally break her out of the fox-masked man’s trance.

Hi there! I wanna share a story on here because I just want it to be known how special this movie is. I was born without a chunk of my hearing and it went undiagnosed until I was in my early twenties. I have never been able to enjoy theaters or concerts or even school plays because of that hearing impairment. I just recently got diagnosed and granted hearing aids. Literally a few months ago. So my friends have been putting together things for me to experience. My favorite childhood movies, musicals (Hamilton is an obsession I didn't think I would have) and even hearing things like footsteps, doors, water and ice. Literally everything. So when it came to my first movie in theaters, it was a really really hard choice. At first I was gonna wait for Iron Lung to come out on streaming or YouTube. But then I saw a video mark posted about just how much work he had put into this movie, how much he had sacrificed and done with his own blood sweat and tears. I'm an aspiring film maker trying to make it in the indie field. I know everyone wants to do that nowadays but I have been on this carrier path since middle school. Hearing what he went through inspired my own career and love for it so much that I decided no other movie was worth hearing in theaters for the first time. Me and my friend saw it in theaters today. I won't spoil it! But it was one of the best experiences in my life and that experience will have a special place in my heart for the rest of my life. 

Thank you for listening to my Ted Talk!

The f or 𝆑 in the title has a few interpretations, and the creators haven't given a straight answer on it.

1. Forte: The way it is stylized is the musical symbol for Forte, meaning a section of music to be played loud or strong. There is a recurring theme of sound in the game with multiple enemies that scream or yell to create damaging or stunning waves, and the sense that Hinako wants to retain her voice (youth, independence) in a time when women are expected to be obedient wives that are seen and not heard. It also contrasts with the "silent" hill name.

2. Five: The last numbered title in the series was Silent Hill 4: The Room. There have been others since, such as Homecoming and Downpour, but if you consider those to be spin-offs and this to be the next true main series game then it would be the fifth. I'd say that's a stretch, but it's a theory that's been thrown around.

3. First: The 1960's setting places this game as the earliest in the franchise's timeline, so it could be considered the first.

4. Female: I don't think this one really has merit, but some people have theorized that it could mean Female since Hinako is the protagonist and the story centers heavily on the expected roles of girls and women in that era.

5. Flower/Forma/Fauna: The fictional flower, Hakkokusou (roughly meaning Memorial or literally translated as State Funeral) is an important part of the story and is speculated to be the origin of the White Claudia, another fictional flower that plays an important part in some of the other Silent Hill games. The Roman roots of the name Claudia can mean lame, limp, waver, or enclosure, so there is a bit of thematic similarity in the names.

6. Fox/Fog/Faith: All important the the story.

7. F to pay respect: Obviously not, but frequently suggested as a joke. I mean, hey, the name of the flower does translate to memorial, right?

A lot of people are saying that Silent Hill F is about leaving childhood behind, but I think there’s more to it than that. The story seems to explore how and why someone might be manipulated into abandoning their innocence. A masked man gradually convinces Hinako that her friends are her enemies, while a symbol of her childhood (the doll) keeps warning her not to trust him. Despite the warnings, she believes him because he seems to care for her, offering validation she can’t find elsewhere. 
Throughout the game, we see lots of imagery related to Hinako’s fears about womanhood, marriage, and motherhood. These fears seem to be based on how she sees her parents’ relationship and the expectations society places on her. The monsters represent this: the doll-like creatures, possibly transformed townsfolk, are elegant but lifeless and mechanical. They're “pretty” objects that exist to be looked at or played with. Hinako even questions whether they were mutilated to keep them from escaping or if they were created solely to suffer that fate. Some only move when seen, like they only have identity or worth when someone’s watching. Another creature licks her and “acts all chummy” with her, a clear metaphor for predation or unwanted sexual attention, especially since “it never bothers with guys.” Then there’s the monster with lots of faces, which cries and vomits everywhere, as if made of children. Its cries overwhelm Hinako, and some versions of it even walk as if playing hopscotch. The birthing, vomiting monster literalizes that horror: the messy, violating transformation of the body and identity that comes with motherhood. The chained, faceless creature feels like loss of self and autonomy, like being bound to a role you can’t escape. And the big creature with the massive blade feels like a manifestation of an abusive husband or father: it's huge, overpowering, always interrupting her attempts to make progress (like when she’s trying to wind the crank at the well). 
Oddly enough, then, there's Sakuko's "evil" angel form. It's also faceless, and Hinako has to fight it in order to follow the fox-masked man. Even as it kills her sometimes, it says things about not wanting to be alone. 
Even the world around her reinforces this. The pale scenery being overtaken by spreading red fungus feels symbolic of womanhood itself, like period blood staining purity. It's simultaneously beautiful and horrifying. It’s a physical manifestation of maturity taking over innocence, creeping forward whether Hinako wants it or not. She’s terrified of it, because the only models of womanhood she’s ever known are defined by suffering, repression, and loss of freedom. The red growth isn’t just blood: it’s inevitability. 
The fox-masked man, then, isn’t simply a villain but a personification of that transition. He doesn't only just pulling Hinako away from her childhood and her friends, but he reshapes her fears to make her dependent on him. He promises safety and understanding but ultimately becomes the agent of her transformation. He represents a false sense of maturity: a predator who disguises control as care. The doll, a relic of her childhood and a symbol of her innocence, keeps warning her there’s no going back once she gives in. The fact that we see it less and less as the story continues feels like her intuition and independence fading away. And Hinako having to go through her memories of her friends only for those very memories to be corrupted feels like the fox-masked man's influence finally starting to take hold. Her memories of her friends in the dream world start out nice, but are slowly corrupted. By the time she's sacrificed all three friends, Hinako's tone is nearly emotionless. It's chilling, but it's like she's let go of her identity. She keeps saying how "it had to be done". That's exactly what the fox-masked man wanted to hear. 
Then the line "I may not see you here... but I know that you are with me"?? That's just creepy. Hinako has become reliant on him, convinced that she's in love. The notes a few episodes ago about Hinako "saving" the fox-masked man and him wanting to take over her body or something (I forget the exact wording) in order to save her just reinforces that. Plus, all of the images of who I can only assume are the fox-mased man's previous victims, all with their faces in their paintings burned off... they lost their identities, too. The she says "I will do what I must... to be the perfect person for you." Her identity is now dependent on him, and she'll go to great lengths to please him, even if she harms herself in the process. Past that point, she obeys whatever the fox-mased man says, speaking monotone, as if mind controlled or brainwashed. Because that's what grooming is. Then, at the end of this episode, all doors are closed to her. I don't know if I'm looking too far into it there, but I've gotten everything about this game from Mark's playthrough because I do not have the reaction time or skill to play it on my own. So rather than being a simple story about leaving childhood behind, Silent Hill F is more like a story of what it means to be forced into adulthood. It's a story about how many women are being groomed, both by a manipulative figure and by societal expectations of womanhood, into a form they never chose for themselves. And that kind of pressure starts young. Sometimes as early as middle school, or even before that.

Like she is trying to escape coming-of-age and fulfilling her societally-expected role and becoming a little housewife/sex object, but she also feels powerless (dodging Shu’s earlier advances, trying to ignore Rinko’s jabs, fighting enemies, generally being a badass). It seems like even by working really hard and being really tough and practically mothering those helpless babies Shu and Rinko, she’s both breaking and fulfilling the role that she’s expected to fall into. That's the thing with puzzle difficulties in Silent Hill, Mark. Shoutout to all the other people who watch Mark play games for the sake of being entertained by his experience with the game, regardless of whether or not he brute forces puzzles. We aren’t here to get upset about him “playing the game wrong”. If you’re wanting to watch someone just play the game perfectly, you’re better off searching for a walkthrough instead. It’s interesting watching a unique perspective of someone playing a game and seeing what information they do and don’t absorb. If you’re getting frustrated watching him play because he isn’t doing things how you expect or want, it might be worthwhile for your own sake to just kick back and try to enjoy the video for what it is: Mark’s experience playing the game. I understand it might upset people when he criticises part of the game even though there are hints given that he misses or doesn’t understand, especially given the difficulty he chose, but it doesn’t HAVE to upset you. It’s like getting upset at someone who gets frustrated that they don’t understand how to do a math problem despite having been taught how. Everyone processes information differently, and his criticisms aren’t meant to be taken as seriously as they sometimes are. They’re just meant to vocalise his personal, non-universal experience.

The 4 meals a day I think represents feeding spotty as well as Leila. The two are practically inseparable in MC's mind, as suggested by the note about Spotty. Therefore when feeding spotty, you may as well be feeding Leila along with him. No normal dog needs to be fed 4 times a day.
This is also what encouraged MC to put Spotty's head on the Mannequin.  MC lost his mind after learning Leila was incurable and dying. The Mannequin was supposed to represent a perfect replacement for Leila after she passed away.
"The years you suffered her" implies the years she has been sick. This changes to 8 later in the game as the MC begins to grow tired of taking care of her, and growing resentful in his grief and insanity; Assuming Leila and the MC have known each other/been together for 8 years. the amount of meals goes down from 4 to 3 as well, after the reality that you did in fact brutally kill Spotty sets in. One less mouth to feed.
The entire theme of metamorphosis is a metaphor for a metastasizing illness, like cancer or something similar. Changing, growing, hardening, becoming more. Leila is enduring a metamorphosis of her illness.
The final stage, "Imago," representing the end goal of the metamorphosis. This word in psychology means an idealized mental image of someone. After Leila's passing, she is freed of the illness that was destroying her body. Leila has no more physical form to hinder the MC's "Imago" of her. She departs for the heavens, as a metaphorical butterfly, and all that is left is the Mannequin. A wooden, unsettling, carved mannequin with a dead dog's rotting head attached to it. A representation of the grief, insanity, and guilt. The flawed Imago.

What a terrifyingly human concept for a horror game. "Two people in love, until one gets too sick" is a tale as old as history. Traditional western marriage vows include the line "in sickness and in health"  for a reason. Of course, we don't consider the weight of that promise. We fail to imagine how difficult it becomes when the sickness is too much. A life partner becomes a burden upon their loved one. Both people can be torn apart by the loneliness, helplessness, frustration, and grief. It's uncomfortable to think about, so we don't. 

I like that this game is from the perspective of the caretaker. They are alone, and have to dedicate all their time tending to Leila's needs. It's a noble endeavor but it destroys their soul. As her condition worsens, the misery felt by the two of them corrupts the caretaker. Imperfections they were once able to overlook, or maybe didn't used to care much about, are now reasons to lash out. Anger is a secondary emotion. People often lose themselves to anger because the root emotion, in this case I believe to be grief, is too painful to linger on. And when you focus on your anger, it intensifies. The caretaker was never a dog person, now they hate that stupid dog and kill it. The anger distorts memories of the past 2 years with Leila and her dog. They start to believe they always hated the dog.  They start to believe they always hated Leila's chubby fingers. Every inconvenience feels gargantuan and deserving of intense rumination. "Leila has too many flaws, if only she was this, if only she was that, I wish I had my perfect Leila, I don't want to see this Leila ever again, this Leila who needs to be fed and watered and medicated and who feels fear and shame and sorrow." They don't want a human anymore, they want a doll, because loving a human requires enduring hardships. They can't take it anymore.

None of this changes the fact that the real victim here is Leila, who has no choice but to rely on her partner to help her, and be betrayed.

The monster isn't the mannequin, or the butterfly, or the disease, or the caretaker. The monster is the weakness of the human heart.

I get *why* they have the quarantine section set up like they do for the game, but it’s also driving me nuts.  Ah yes, let’s put all the possibly healthy people with possibly sick people!  All in a single chamber with no barriers or guards!

Edit: yes, I understand the possible reasons WHY the dev made it a single, tiny chamber (literally the first thing I said).  It’s a demo, limitations of the dev’s own time/resources, game mechanics, in-game resources/lore, etc.  What I was trying to express was that a quarantine setup like this wouldn’t work (in a zombie apocalypse or irl) and it was bugging me because it’s a stupid thing to do when you’re trying to keep as many people as possible healthy (in a zombie apocalypse or irl).
Since I’m already adding more to this post, here’s some things I personally think could be changed.  Switch the quarantine building and our character’s quarters (no seriously, why is it so big and bright… I get it, we’re a “commander” or something but we do literally every job except command), put a single guard inside, and have 2-4 cots or chairs that the people sent to quarantine are tied to.  Would still make sense why they’re so pissed/scared while there, no one likes being tied up against their will.  If someone was infected, have where there’s a chance they could break free and kill everyone (including the guard, which could make future days more difficult), and have the chance of them breaking free increase as the game continues (wear and tear would make items less durable, and the lack of resources means you’d have to make do with whatever you can).
Speaking of resources, if there’s issues with supply or there’s some sort of corruption/funneling of resources elsewhere, they need to indicate that more.  The survivor area and lack of guards is a good start.  They even mention that the Insta-Zombie Identifier has limited use.  But then we’re given unlimited ammo and can call in an airstrike, and there’s two entire trucks to pick up 5 people?  Cool idea for protecting the camp and convoy, and I can see how the truck selection could be fun once the game is finished, but it also tells me that there is no lack of resources.  Sure, maybe the group in control decided to allocate more resources into killing zombies, in which case there needs to be some sort of indication of that (the guards or civilians gossiping, an email or note from whoever was in charge before you, etc).  Maybe this whole camp is actually supposed to act like bait for a giant trap, that would be a fun idea.  As for protecting the camp/convoy, could be changed to where each bullet costs quite a bit or the more bullets/airstrikes you use, the more favors you have to do for higher ups (let this specific person through, kill this person, etc).  You can fill up a truck with 20 people, but there’s only one truck.  At first, very few zombies are wandering around and rarely attack the camp.  But the more active the camp is (more people, more generators used, the more often you use an airstrike, etc), the more zombies there are wandering around the camp and actively attacking.  If you fill up the truck(s) too much, more zombies will try to attack the convoy (also if the trucks are indestructible to an airstrike, then I’m sure they can tank a couple of zombies).  The bait you can use (that didn’t really… work) would make much more sense then.  The idea of using a drone is cool too, but just have it be a guy on the wall when the camp is attacked and someone in the truck during the escort.  Does the exact same thing but with more limitations and I don’t have to keep wondering where the energy to charge a drone is coming from.
I could keep going, there’s many things that could be done to make the game more believable (as much as it can be for a zombie apocalypse game) while still making it fun or difficult.  And that’s not to say that the game doesn’t have good stuff, I really like the idea of doing a medical examination on these people, learning more and more about symptoms of this virus, having to weigh the risks of someone turning into a zombie versus them just being sick.  I would love to play it once it’s fully released, though I hope that the dev makes some changes.
TLDR I know what game mechanics and resources are, and there’s some stuff that could be changed in the game that would make it more enjoyable/immersive.  I just didn’t think anyone would breeze past “I get *why*” and then decide to comment about how I clearly don’t understand how games or the real world works.  Silly me!
(For those of you being respectful while stating your opinions/thoughts about the “why,” I appreciate you and that last bit was not aimed at you ❤)

I think the really important thing with those static moments, when you’re stuck in the bed and all you can do is look around, is that it NEEDS to progress. You can do this in 2 ways, either it progresses around you whether you look or not, things happen and it’s up to the player to engage with them, or the player is responsible for continuing the scene by looking but you HAVE to have really obvious cues. Tapping on the window, clattering, obvious scary directional noise. And honestly that noise is really important even if it progresses without player input because it encourages the player to look where you want. I really hope the devs learn from this and implement these things and work on their pacing, because the atmosphere of that bedroom was nailed, it was creepy… until it wasn’t.

Spoiler free tips;
1. You can’t process the tapes until you’ve bought upgrades.
2. The drone is offline as the text box shows, u need to climb the radio tower and turn it back on as it occasionally shuts down.
3. You can break wood with rocks it just takes forever, crowbar and other things are better.
4. You can click the dials to tune the signals and scroll wheel while you look away, as long as u continue to hold your left click down. U don’t need to keep turning them on and off and looking away. Just left click, look up, scroll to turn up and down, and then scroll back to 0 when u get as close to 100% as u can. 
5. ALT+R will set things down. There’s an area in the tutorial area that will really break down all of them different controls for throw, drop, and hold item.
6. You are playing a heavily out of date version. Even the newest version I haven’t tried yet but you are missing some key items and things in the base that make the game better, I won’t say what, but there’s much more. 
7. You cant  actually damage tapes by slamming them around, it’s just noise and visuals for fun. The tape u had was uploaded to the processor but couldn’t be processed and you never put it back on the tape so you just lost it after you put another on top of it, overwriting it.

Essentially in this game you need to process signals, make money, upgrade stuff, all while maintaining your base servers, satellite servers, generators and other things. The base servers and satellite servers are separate things, so u need to check if they are active or not on the terminal regularly.

33:03 important note here: there’s a stark contrast between dedicated tools being developed by health professionals and the usage of Silicon Valley’s GenAI trained on medical data. Mark’s right, but I want to provide more context as someone working in public health.

Peer-reviewed studies of GenAI application in diagnosis haven’t been very optimistic, even if headlines and tweets keep saying “it correctly diagnoses more often than doctors.” In reality, a specifically-trained model scored just barely better against doctors on a “closed-book” no-reference test, while doctors scored significantly better on the second, open-book round of testing. The third round included a section for doctors and the model to describe “why” the answer they selected was correct, and that’s where the issue reared its head: doctors consistently had sound reasoning, and if they weren’t correct they were close, but the model just made things up and would sometimes be technically correct for very wrong reasons.

Mark’s right here: the tech, if better-researched (and specifically if it’s NOT coming from this cohort of Silicon Valley weirdos), could have HUGE positive implications for many scientific fields. Other tools in the neighborhood of similar tech have already revolutionized data analysis in several fields, and there’s a great use-case to *assist* doctors in diagnosis and examine data to identify systemic disparities in health outcomes.

The problem with this tech is that its current stewards and profiteers are scumbags, liars, plagiarists, and disproportionately in favor of some of the worst politics you could imagine. Taking the car keys away from them and centering ethics in continued research is the only safe way to move forwards.

The easiest way I have found to fathom just how much Ai does not think when in generates text, is by looking at the “next word” options above the phone keyboard. Does my phone know where I’m taking my sentence? No, it just calculates what is most likely going to be the next word I use based on the word before it. It doesn’t understand anything, it just calculates probabilities. No matter how advanced Ai gets, no matter the scale, it’s still just moving blocks of unknowable information around until the calculations say “Yep, that’s probably it.” It doesn’t think, it doesn’t understand, it’s just a blind robot putting a puzzle together using only a calculator. It’s just gotten so fast at its calculations, that it’s convinced people it can see.

Mark you will love "Still Lies The Deep." It's a beautiful horror game about the sea but also human resilience. It does take some skill, but with your FNAF background you'll have fun getting through all the areas and different monsters. 

Everyone I've seen play this game has loved it and said it has stuck with them. The last game I've seen make this much of an impact on the Internet was Mouthwashing. 

This games is a piece of art made with so much authenticity and passion, I promise this one will stay with you. It's a love letter to the hundreds of people who lived that reality. It's a snap shot of a time and place in history important to it's country, yet not as well know I'm other West countries. It's still relevant today. 

It already has a DLC that creators are playing and playing and posting  videos of. 

I know you don't have a lot of free time and you have a list of games to play, but even if you play it just for yourself, I think it's worth it.

 In today's Distractible episode you guys talked about how shit big game companies are now and how embarrassing their releases are. You talked about how indie games or games made by small teams are monumentally overwhelming triple A games, and of these Still Wakes The Deep is one of the best.

It's epic. It's so gorgeous and memorable. I compare it to Death Stranding when it first came out and we were all shocked at how amazing it looked. 

Maybe I'm exaggerating a bit, but I champion this game because I believe it's a Beacon demanding upon others to rise up. To create other monumental, titan games to stand above, upholding the only standard of games we will accept. To stand above the thick, disgusting smog these big companies ooze and fester in, while  gathering their filth to craft their shit games. 

Happy birthday Mark, and gift yourself grace and happiness. Play if you are happy, and play what will make you happy.

In Sister Location, the first mainline FNAF game to experiment with more mobility than just ‘point-and-click’, there was one moment in that game, one key event that tied it all together. No hype moment to let us reminisce about how the franchise started. No callback to the series origins. Like Mark said, the games are good. Everything is (reasonably) polished, the stories are decent, and the gameplay is fun. Honestly i kinda agree with mark's take on the new FNAF games.

Like yeah, they're not inherently bad. They're decent horror games. But to me, it feels like the essence of FNAF games is gone ever since security breach. It stopped being about interesting and new mechanics where you had to survive in an enclosed space, fending off creatures; and more about "Hide from x threat while doing y objective. Also here you have some hiding holes/spaces where you're basically safe. Oh and don't forget about scripted chase sequence. OK now it's gonna happen 5 more times." It has become a generic horror game. Mark has also pointed something about these out: the chase sequences are only fun the first time you play them. After the first time, you know exactly what's going to happen and what you need to do to survive. And in a game like this, where you have to literally replay the whole thing again to get a different ending, it gets tedious. Almost like a chore.

I feel like they could do something so good and interesting with the old formula of cams and offices, now that there's a whole studio and enough budget. I would love a game of this caliber, where you had to survive in different offices, with different map layouts and mechanics (but not too different or hard between each other), all on the same game. No scripted chase scenes, just full-on survive the night (or designated time) where the animatronic threats behave on randomly generated patterns (RNG) on each try.

Obviously I can foresee that my idea has its' inherent flaws, but I don't wanna play hide-and-seek with Monster nºX and then have it chase me through strictly linear chase sequences. For the fourth time. Over.

It hits that uncanny valley perfectly

Monster explanation for dummies:
1) You can't hurt it. I know you have a gun and your Ooga Booga brain automatically goes "I'm gonna start blasting",
But you CANNOT hurt it. You shooting the monster in the head does nothing.
2) The monster is afraid of light, that's why you have a Flare Gun and not a Double Barrel Shotgun. In other words... Light the path.
3) You don't HAVE to use the flare gun, you can just run. The monster's chase is timed, if you outrun it or go far enough away it will despawn. It also can't go inside tight spaces like vents.

For people who don't know about this, at 1:01:26 there's an alternate path you can take that leads to one of my favorite secret zones in this game. Rather than climbing into the vent like Mark did in the video, you'd need to climb to the opening in the ceiling until you reach a grate that is slightly open. In order to access the zone, you need a "blink eye" (which is an item you can unlock by using it twice in endless substructure after escaping the teeth guy) and use it to teleport past the grate and fall down the vent. In my opinion, this zone is by far the most challenging and scariest part of the game, but it's also my favorite because of those reasons.

A couple tips for this game: 
1.) Schedule all of your dead drops and deals for late night, past 12 am. You no doubt noticed that time doesn't pass after 4 am. This means any deals you schedule in that time period won't ever expire (they say they expire at 6 am, but you won't reach 6am until you sleep). That way you can do all your shopping and transport and recruiting customers and dealers during the day, and take as long as you want or need to complete your deals at 4 am. That also means you can spend as long as you want cleaning up the whole town once the deals are done lol. 
2.) This one isn't relevant for this playthrough anymore, but it is possible to take everything out of the trailer before it blows up. If you ever play this game from the start again, keep that in mind. The UV grow pots are mid-game items and getting them at the start can give you a massive boost.

Also a couple tips because I see the entire comment section FUMING over this (and rightfully so): (somewhat spoiler alert - mark hasn't realised these things not lore spoilers or content spoilers)

1. YOU HAVE AN INVENTORY MARK where you can store all those shiny items u have been throwing immediately after finding them (press Tab and store em in that big transparent popup menu). Storing too many hinders your jump however as you are too heavy.

 - kill those bugs you hate so much or deter certain OTHER entities...

- break the wood planks as shown in the tutorial

4. BUGS are the currency and is what you are meant to deposit in all of the vending machines. Golden ones are worth 1, Silver bugs are worth 5. RED bugs explode on contact, hence why something 'exploded' in the pipe. Brown bugs are useless. 
5. In the PAID version, that same computer you find in that interlude area you use to insert a disk in also provides a single PERKS/UPGRADES such as stamina, climb speed, hammer strength etc.

1:42:25  So the "Markiplier Curse" is actually a real thing that a lot of people have, and it isn't that you "do worse" after your first attempt, it's that your strats change after your first attempt.  The first attempt you play more slowly and cautiously to gather information, and on later attempts you try to actualize that information.  

"Worse" is an inherently subjective term, and while he isn't getting the boss' health as low, he's doing more damage per second, which is harder to do.  He's using a higher skill requirement strat after learning the basics of the boss encounter.

It's similar to the idea of "beginners luck."  When you're new at something every action is intentional, but when you are experienced many actions are reflexive, and situations that are unusual may prompt the wrong reflex at the wrong time.

Part of the crew loses their minds and begins worshiping the threat.  They provided sacrifices and are resorting to cabalism.  Main character has had both legs and an arm torn off, carries on, and proceeds to almost single handedly take the threat out himself.  That is some crazy levels of will to live.

I think one of the differences in the vibe of Endoparasitic 1 and 2 is the presentation of the enemies. In 1, many of them are drawn to show they are standing; they're person-sized and upright, and quite large in some cases, especially the teleporting ones and the boss. You feel overwhelmed by being outmatched by something bigger and more mobile than you are. In 2, everything is down at Cynte's level; the standard mutants are a person twisted sideways to crawl like a crab, the stray limbs, and the little fuzzy guys that react to light, they're all low to the ground. Even the invisible creatures don't seem to be very big given the size of the subtle distortion they create when onscreen. This presentation plus Cynte's experience makes things feel more evenly matched, you're not as desperate and outmatched, you're a man on a mission. 

The framing of the boss fight, with Adorned One Luce below the catwalks, with Cynte/the player looking down at her, contributes to this more action-y feeling. Although part of the intention is probably to show off the design of the whole creature, her movements could have been telegraphed in other ways, like casting a shadow from above with the player below her. I think it's a fair shift in tone, but I agree that leaning more on the environmental storytelling versus conversation and monologue does make the story feel a tad weaker than the first game. All in all the team and the VAs did a fantastic job! (Also with the thought that everything is down at Cynte's level, we have to acknowledge the minor comedy that a person standing up would probably see a handful of balloons bobbing angrily around the furniture before they noticed Cynte...)

Those invisible dudes take 7 shots from your pistol since you can't hit them in the head, at least Mark couldn't. However, they only take 2 shotgun bullets and you always make the shotgun shells in increments of 2, so you're not losing anything but you're also not gaining anything either. There's never that many in a level, if you have 4 shells in the chamber and 6 on hand, you should have an easier time dispatching them and you won't be losing so much pistol ammo.

I feel like it ought to be said: This isn't really a backrooms game. It's a perfectly servicable haunted house game about a murder and guilt, which is set in the Backrooms, probably to justify making the decoration very sparse in places. It quickly moves past the horror of the lonely, infinite, bare, liminal setting to make the player go through a bunch of fairly standard spooky setpieces, and I think the comparison to Layers of Fear is telling. That doesn't necessarily make it a bad game, I just think it's heavily mislabelling itself when it's hardly about the backrooms at all.

Some tips (that you probably won't see):
1. The shotgun guy is blind, he follows sound, so you have to be quiet when he's near
2. You can crouch and hide under things like tables to escape some of the monsters
3. When you revive someone, they come back with 1 HP, and you can give them health by -backshots- clicking on their back, by the health bar
4. IIRC that baby works like an enderman? so don't stare at it and it won't hurt you
5. You can't have two extraction points open at the same time, so trying to open the second one and save the first won't work
6. You can pick up the gnomes and break them so they die
7. The ducks won't hurt you if you don't touch them, they just follow you
8. You can carry things like weapons that you purchase from the shop in your inventory (the 1, 2, 3 slots at the bottom middle of the screen) so you don't have to always be holding them

There’s definitely room for improvement. 

1: his walk animation should be more of violent limp, less like a waddle and more like he’s using all of his effort to push forward with his broken robotic limbs. 

2: people have already mentioned this but this game needs actual hiding spots. Examples would be storage lockers, fold up dining tables with large hanging tablecloths to hide under, or maybe even piles of scrap and wreckage. When hiding in these spots springtrap should be unable to find you unless you make a fairly large amount of noise. If springtrap is already chasing you after spotting you, the hiding spots shouldn’t work unless you’re around a corner out of his direct line of sight when you enter the hiding spot.

3: work on the jump scare. Jump scares are annoying when the feel cheap and unearned, but a player that knows how to play the game has plenty of time to know when the jump scare is coming. The jump scare being a completely avoidable punishment for making a mistake prevents the jump scare from feeling as cheap, so it’s ok for it to be scary instead of relying entirely on tension.

4: Springtrap should be fast when he spots you, but maybe not quite that fast, being spotted should be something that you can survive if you’re skilled enough. I think the player should be fast enough to outrun springtrap for around 5  to 7 seconds if sprinting. This can be balanced out with a stamina bar, the stamina shouldn’t last long if the player sprints without stopping. It can be immersion breaking if the player character is unable to power walk for more than 10 seconds without having to stop and catch their breath, but it can be easily explained if the player character is somehow injured during the intro. The stamina mechanic can become more complex and interesting if it is used for more than sprinting though.

5: building off of the stamina mechanic, there are a few things I can imagine using stamina for. If the character is established in the intro to be injured, it would make sense for some hiding spots to use stamina when you enter them as your character needs to push rubble aside before hiding behind it or something along those lines. There could also be doors that are blocked by fallen objects or rubble, and can only be opened by spamming space bar or something to push it open. One last thing, it would add to the panic and tension if Springtrap’s jumpscare was something you could break out with using some kind of quick time event at the cost of a large portion of stamina. This would give the jumpscare more of a pay off because the player would be panicking in the moment before they’re killed.

Managing the symptoms of ADHD with Powerwash Simulator is so real

I'm not even exaggerating when I say that game has fundamentally made me rethink how I approach basically *any* task

it's also been really empowering for myself and other people that I preach its splendours to.

The way that you tackle things in PowerWash is that you come into something that looks impossible and immediately your brain wants to turn away and do something else because it's too much time and effort, but the more that you play, you more you realise just how modular everything is and that breaking these mega tasks down into smaller goal posts is legitimately really helpful for just life itself. Sure, the goal is to "clean the back garden", but really it's broken down into sub tasks like "clean the pond" or "clean the chair" or "clean the table". You just move from small task to small task and before you know it, you've spent 14 hours cleaning a subway station. There's some bigger areas to clean that don't fall into the usual categories of cleaning like, a grill, or a van door, but you teach yourself to deal with these obstacles in your own way. Me personally, if I'm powerwashing the floor I'll slice it off into chunks and clear out each little area instead of trying to tackle the whole thing at once.

One thing that's really empowering about playing PowerWash Simulator is how well its ethos translates to all manners of tasks. I tell people all the time that if you can play PowerWash Simulator (especially with ADHD) you can be an artist, a game developer, a musician, a dancer; because PowerWash Simulator, silly as it sounds, contains most of the tools you'll need to take on any task or learn any discipline.

Anyways, here's Fnaf lore:


William Afton and Henry Emily opened a restaurant around the early 70s, named Fredbear's Family Diner, which quickly evolved into a chain of restaurants known as "Freddy Fazbear's Pizza," started in 1983, under the company of Fazbear Entertainment, Inc. At some point, both of them left the company, with an unknown individual taking over as CEO.

William was secretly a serial killer, using mascot costumes to lure, abduct, and murder kids. His motives aren't known, though widely speculated to be him trying to achieve immortality through researching the paranormal, haunted metal (known as remnant), which he created through the murders.

His first target was Charlotte Emily, the daughter of Henry. She became the Marionette, a ghost who took care of and helped awaken the other lost souls.

In 1983, William's younger son also died in an incident, at the fault of his eldest — Michael. The younger son (name unknown, BV for short) 's fate is still unknown, though often speculated to be connected to either Golden Freddy (an enigmatic spirit taking the form of a yellow bear) or helping Charlie with saving other souls. "I will put you back together" was the last thing said to BV by a debatable party, most commonly believed to be either William, Charlie, or Golden Freddy.

In 1985, William killed 2 kids, and 3 others were later connected to that incident (The Missing Children Incident, or MCI). He was arrested but released due to a lack of evidence. 4 of these kids were Gabriel, Susie, Little Jeremy, and Fritz, going on to haunt Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy, respectively, with Susie implied to have been the first to die. The 5th is commonly believed to be named Cassidy, becoming Golden Freddy, though some think it's someone else.

In 1987, William pretended to be a security guard at a new Pizzeria and killed 5 more kids (DCI for short), who went on to be the Toy animatronics. This caused the unimportant Bite of '87.

In 1993, Mike worked a shift at the haunted original Freddy's. Later that year, the location was closed, and the company went bankrupt. He later had some sort of nightmares about it and his brother's death, likely paranormal in nature.

At some point, William went to that original Freddy's to destroy the 4 haunted robots, but ghosts manifested, and fearing for his life, he put on the costume he used to kill them. It was actually a part costume part robot hybrid, though, and due to the leaking roof, the machine snapped on him, killing him. He went on to haunt it and/or his corpse inside.

While Freddy's existed, a Sister Location called "Circus Baby's Pizza World" opened. It was a front for William to kill more kids, with the robots there made to kidnap them. It backfired when his daughter sneaked in to see Baby, and it killed her. She then haunted it. William, distraught, locked her and the other robots from there in an underground warehouse where they were rented out for parties. The other robots also got haunted somehow, likely with melted down remnant from some other kids, most likely MCI. Years later, William sent Mike there to find Elizabeth. Thinking he was William, she tricked him, and the Funtime Robots combined into one amalgam of wires, killed Mike, and used his corpse as a skin suit to escape. He quickly rotted, and they had to escape to the sewers. He repossessed his corpse thanks to remnant, though.

Around 30 years after his death (presumably 2023, though that may be debunked now), William was found by Phone Dude, who stole him and put him into his cheap horror attraction based on the Freddy's urban legends, not knowing William was inside the robot. After a few nights, the building burned down, and William escaped. There's also a good ending in that game where Charlie released the other spirits, but its canonicity is "complicated" according to Scott (FNaF creator).

Mike also had a security logbook at some point, where two ghosts, BV and presumably Cassidy (given it's not him), talked about something.

Finally, after like 50 years, Henry re-emerged and made a fake pizzeria, where he called the Funtime robots, now separated from Elizabeth, herself, and William. He also made a robot that captured Charlie. After a bunch of managers failed to collect all 4 robots, Mike came and succeeded. Henry burned them all and himself, with high temperatures now revealed to work on ghosts, apparently. Fazbear Entertainment, Inc. was supposedly closed for good.

But one ghost, very highly implied to be Golden Freddy, though argued as a random never-before-seen 6th MCI kid by some, wasn't ready to let William go, so he kept him from being released and tortured him in super nightmares.

There's a book series called Fazbear Frights which has debatable canonicity too that'd take place after this, but if canon it's basically just filler that nullifies the Vengeful Spirit nightmares thing.

After all this, Fazbear Entertainment was revived as Fazbear Entertainment, LLC. They kidnapped a guy and gaslighted him into living in a secluded fake house they made for him, where he made FNAF games, in the FNaF universe, as to make it seem like it was all just fake stories.

A VR game was later made, that was a remake of these, but some suspecious circuit boards were sent to be scanned into it, creating a paranormal, digital entity known as Glitchtrap. It appears as a man in Spring Bonnie (William's suit), acts exactly like William, knows stuff only William knows and even claims to be back, with William's catchphrase of sorts being "I always come back". After a bit of shenanigans, it manages to possess a beta tester and makes her his minion. We call her Vanny.

Vanessa, most likely Vanny, then got a desk job at Fazbear Entertainment. Fazbear Funtime Service, a program where animatronics were mass produced and sent for parties, etc. got hijacked by Glitchtrap who made them hostile. He made Vanessa infiltrate the service as a fake FazEnt representative, supposedly fix his infection, but actually just cut off anyone's access to the system other than him, and send a data packet with him to the current Pizzeria — Freddy Fazbear's Mega Pizzaplex.

In the current book series, most likely canon, there's this AI called Mimic1, which copies stuff. Many think that's actually what Glitchtrap is, just AI copying William. It's an ongoing debate. An Endoskeleton with it installed was sent to the last simulated Freddy's Henry built to burn, where it got out of control, started killing people and in the ongoing story is hunting down a group of teens. As the Pizzaplex was built on top of the simulated Freddy's, the Mimic got control over it too, but was quickly taken down. There's also this boy Gregory who ended up possessed by Glitchtrap and hacking the Pizzaplex for reasons unknown.

Now in Security Breach (possibly 2035), Gregory, out of Glitchtrap's control, had to escape being trapped in the Pizzaplex, as all the robots controlled by Glitchtrap and Vanny wanted to kill him. With the help of Glamrock Freddy, most likely haunted by someone, though it's unknown who, Greg ended up finding a newly built Springtrap in the simulated Freddy's and somehow defeating it. There's also a giant abomination of wires that resambles the Funtime amalgam down there, it took this William away.

35:37 in regards to Blackboard + stones, *all* stones count against Blackboard regardless of underlying suit. Blackboard specifies a hand with *only* spades+clubs, and stone cards, counting as no suit, are not spades/clubs and therefore turn it off.

This wording does mean, though, that with no cards in hand, Blackboard still triggers. All the (0) cards have either spades or clubs as their suit, after all.

That is the limit the player character can carry (with a bag, too) before he becomes immeasurably slow. (The theory he starved himself on purpose for the weight limit is backed up by two things: the fact that he had to leave all his weapons behind _while starved_ to meet the weight limit, despite how light some of those weapons may be, implying just how tight the weight limit was; as well as the fact that he survived for 3 months in the facility, implying it is well stocked on food, which makes sense considering he seemingly had no visitors of any kind in those 3 months. Remember, you need to place your jokers in a specific order to maximize their abilities. They're basically like a math equation. Any joker that gives extra chips, go to the left, jokers that add to the multiplyer stay in the middle, jokers that multiply to the multipyer stay to the right. E.g. +5 chips, +30chips, +4mult, +8 mult, x2mult (5+30)x(4+8)x2. Also, if you run out of discards and need to get rid of more, try adding them to your played hand if you hand is less than the maximum of 5. E.g. you're playing a pair, take the opportunity to trash 3 (or less) unwanted cards, or if you're playing a 2 pair, trash one card.

You did pretty well for the tutorial level and having nothing unlocked. Just a reminder there is a difference between ADDING mult and MULTIPLYING mult.

In terms of which one to focus on, either the blue chips or the red mult, its usually better to focus on the mult since either one results in the same amount, but the red is the only one that can increase via multiplication

Few tips:
1. -1 ante, -1 hand is good for when you are struggling. You can essentially give yourself more time to prep for the late game since the amount of chips you need to score will be lower in the lower antes.
2. When you buy vouchers it unlocks the possibility for an upgraded version of the voucher to show up in the store. So maybe the blank voucher does nothing? how do you upgrade nothing?
3. If you have a bad hand, play your best option but still make sure to play 5 cards. You might only score with 2 of the cards you played but you'll discard all 5 meaning you get to draw 5 new cards.

When Mita first introduces herself at 4:36 it says "Hi, I'm Mita", but she says "はじめまして" (Hajimemashite) which basically is the wording you use to greet somebody and it's like a "pleased to meet you" or "How do you do?"  for pleasantries. Like, a self-introduction.

Normally, you'd say something like "はじめまして。私わ (Your name)です。どうぞよろしく。" 
"(Hajimemashite. Watashi wa (Your name) desu. Douzo Yoroshiku.)"

Which basically means, "Hi/Pleased to meet you. I am (Your name).  Pleased to meet you."

Both Hajimemashite and Douzo Yoroushiku basically mean the same thing "Pleased to meet you", but for correct grammar, you'd put Douzo Yoroushiku at the END of the sentence and Hajimemashite at the BEGINNING of your sentence. 

I'm still learning Japanese, so if anyone Japanese is willing to correct me, please do. 😊❤❤❤

Since there's been some comments on what happened to the creator, here's a detailed breakdown on what went on:

NyankoBfLol's discord account was hacked and his own server got deleted. When the hacker got into his account, he posted racial slurs and sent very unusual messages to his friends. Then the hacker leaked Nyanko's face, name, and family pictures online. He also hacked a second account of Nyanko's which had a lot of his work and games on it. They've all been deleted. 

Apparently this was caused by the fact that the Sprunki mod got so popular, it completely overshadowed the game it was modded on. Incredibox became known for Sprunki and someone took issue with that. It's why the creator isn't pleased to have Mark making a video about it, Sprunki getting more popular than Incredibox was what started this situation, and now it may get even more popular thanks to Mark.

Edit: This isn’t a criticism of Mark, nobody can expect him to be aware of any drama happening with every game he checks out. 

Edit 2: Also important to note that Mark (accidentally) played the wrong version. This version of the game on Itchio is stolen, which is probably why there was no description. The website Mark went to later on was fake. 

Sources: Most recent community post from Nyanko, the description of the most recent video from him, and 2 Reddit threads in the Sprunki subreddit. CONTEXT!! (surely Mark will never see this but still)
Sprunki is a mod for the game Incredibox, a game where you have a list of characters (5 beats, 5 effects, 5 melodies and 5 voices, from top left to bottom right respectively) and usually 7 polos (the guys where you place the characters). This last year a new genre was created in this game's community, horror games, these were simple, just scary guys with scary sounds, but recently a lot of new mods appeared with some interesting mechanics, from a horror mode after a after a specific character (like Sprunki), give you a book with lore that explains something about every character (usualy how they died or something about they like their relationships with other characters), some sort of boss battle (there's a mod where you can't do too much noise because that will wake a creature in the background), and a LARGE etc. There are a LOT of horror mods. The one that started everything was Orin Ayo, a mod made in the coding plataform Scratch, the story was simple, some sort of limbo with a lot of people that died in terrible ways. FYI if anyone is interested - the whole game is about Samosbor - SCPesque Russian literature phenomenon about monsters, anomalies etc. Basically the building guys are in IS Samosbor, which is a lovcraftian apartment building we call 'Панельки' or 'Панельные дома', which were implemented by president Khrushchev to battle housing crisis. All those buildings are the same essentially, which was the whole point - to produce templated apartments, that can be put together quick. 

Except Samosbor, which roughly translates to "Self-assembler" is one of those templated buildings, but it keeps growing. Upwards, downwards, what have you. It is in all actuallity infinite. And people just stuck there. One day they were living in their flat on Novokuznetskaya street in the middle of Moscow, next thing they know - they're in Samosbor. 

Rather creepy, is what I'm saying.
