Okay Mark, Im going to explain this game’s story and lore.
So this game takes place between fnaf 6 and security breach. Shown by the stuff in vanny’s secret room  and the charge station we see burntrap in. She’s in the process of restoring afton (burntrap) by infusing his damaged body with remnant, which is basically soul energy. To do that she’s set up this “attraction” designed to entrap people so she can extract remnant from them. The reason the player character receives the message telling them to check out the “attraction” in the game’s opening cutscene  is because someone that had the player character’s phone number had gone to the attraction and was killed for their remnant and their phone was used to lure more  people they had in their contacts to the “attraction”  that’s why the victims are instructed to bring all their stuff so vanny can get their phones in order to lure new victims for more remnant that’s why we see another person getting sent the text inviting them to the attraction at the end. At the end when you see a hand flash between a human and a endoskeleton’s is becuase the player character’s remnant was taken and infused into afton because you essentially had your soul stolen and now you’re forever trapped in someone else’s body with no control unless afton finally dies. Also a sidenote it would’ve been impossible to get all of the original animatronics from all the previous games/locations because the funtimes and baby were burned in the fnaf 6 fire and are now part of the blob  in security breach  and the nightmares aren’t real. So the reason it looks that way is sound illusion disks (a concept from the 2nd book the twisted ones) they work by emitting sounds at a certain frequency that tricks the human brain into perceiving things differently this is evidenced when the vent door hit “springtrap” at the end of the fnaf 3 segment it seemingly glitched into a regular endo meaning the disk must’ve gotten damaged by the impact causing the player character to see the animatronic’s actual appearance which is that of a bare endo it’s safe to assume this applies to every animatronic in the attraction save for the staff bots at the start and burntrap.

I can't be the only one that feels like the story feels hollow here, right? Like there are good things: the idea of the ink world leaking out into reality, the ideas of the gent corporation being this sort of industrial antagonist figure, the idea behind what Audrey is, I think all of that is cool and could be very interesting. The presentation leaves things feeling sort of empty. Audrey clearly has some sort of amnesia seeing as she forgot who her father is, but outside of that context it's not made very clear and feels weirdly out of place. Serious moments like Wilson saying he plans to basically sacrifice Audrey are undercut by more goofy things, like the sailor cartoon drawing he plans on basically turning her into just looking silly, a tense moment that you can't help but laugh at. The main things that made me want to bring this up are Joey's line about "you don't just need a pencil and a dream, you need heart" and Audrey's monologue in the end. They feel like the kind of thing someone would write for a grand finale, but it just feels forced. Audrey suddenly acting like she had some character arc about taking control of her father's fictional pocket dimension, when she's spent most of the game just nervously going with the flow, feels like whoever was writing the plot assumed that a boss fight and a speech was all she needed to grow as a person.

From what I can tell, this game is a commentary on the nature of creating fictional works. Audrey's father wants her to carry on with his legacy, continuing to make works using his characters. Wilson wants to introduce a completely new character for her to work with, one she doesn't have any previous connection with. The ink demon represents her un-aimed creativity and lack of inspiration; she has talent, but she doesn't know what to do with it. The finale represents her finally finding her purpose in continuing to work with the characters her father first came up with. All she had to do was pour her soul into it, to to do it.

For anyone who doesn't know, that clicking in the hallway and the apartments that starts at 9:12 ish, that's a japanese horror trope revolving around boxcutters. Since weapons are largely outlawed and heavily regulated, the most common weapon used is a boxcutter since you can get those from work at a lot of jobs. They show up in a lot of japanese media, but that clicking in particular is someone extending and retracting the blade repeatedly. I've seen a few japanese horror games use it and knowing what it is only makes it 10x scarier.

Also, the fact that it lines up with the light in the room is supposed to make you go "Oh, maybe it's just the light."

I just rewatched Mark playing the first game and this episode has SO MANY references!

- The head with the eye that follows you used to be the head creator/designer of what was supposed to be Joey Drew’s theme park. Somehow, he embedded his spirit into a ride for the park and the head was in the middle. He was one of the bosses that Henry had to fight and break down.

- HENERY OBVIOUSLY. At the end of the first game, the cycle resets, only it seems that this time, the Keepers and Wilson were a part of it. Instead of Henry resetting the cycle again with the “The End” reel, it seems that after Wilson took it over, he couldn’t have the same thing happening, and had the Keepers capture him.

- I’m gonna take a wild guess and say that the cell with the words “Are you worthy to walk with angels?” (or something like that) used to hold a version of Alice Angel that was much like the first game’s antagonist, and wanted to make herself “beautiful” again. I haven’t watched the other parts, but I think it’s safe to assume that we’ll reencounter a different Alice Angel (or the one that’s been helping Audrey). It could also be that the cell held Suzie, the voice actor for Alice Angel in the cartoons, who blurred the lines between reality and fiction, believing herself to be the true Alice Angel.

- THE FINAL CELL HAS SAMMY LAWRENCE! If you need a refresher, Sammy Lawrence, according to the Archives from “Bendy and the Ink Machine” was a fan favorite with the release of the second chapter. Lawrence was a musician, and was responsible for so many of Joey Drew’s music. Alas, he was subjected to the ink, and in an attempt to spare himself, tried to sacrifice Henry to the Ink Demon. He’s also a boss that Henry had to fight, but Tom kills and/or stops him from killing Henry. Also, I think it’s cool that he had his Bendy mask off and was playing his lil guitar :D

1:34: "...und Du Kannst kein Deutsch gesprechen," is German for "...and you can't speak German!"
          Markiplier's follow-up statement that it was 'the worst German anyone's ever spoken, that his papa (baba?) would not be proud of him just sells it!' 😆
Plus the Eerie Music House scenario is pretty much  an obvious reference (like so much of this game) to H.P. Lovecraft's writing, more specifically, Lovecraft's story 'The Music of Erich Zann,' which was about a strange German man who played the violin (or cello, I dunno it's been years) whose rationale for why he plays the music (to keep the universe from being destroyed by some malevolent force that existed beneath the apartment where he lived) is the same. As is the un-plot twist that the musician wasn't just insane from years dedicated to his craft, there _is_ an unspeakable evil that is kept tame by his talent, and is erased from our reality the moment the protagonist, who views himself as the voice of reason and normality in a Lovecraft story (which is always doomed to fail because they couldn't read the room, pick up on the weirdness, or because they tried to deny it) manages to talk him into taking a break for once in his life, out of a well-intentioned desire to help an obviously obsessed and neurotic fella.

5:35: It's a reference to a line in Stephen King (or at least, Stanley Kubrick's version of it)'s _The Shining_ , with the repeated line of "All Work and No Play Makes Jack a Dull Boy." Guess what 'Arbeit' and 'Spiel' are German for? You don't get any points because I just explained it.

12:05: ...but you got a sweet crystal! Besides, we barely knew that strange cello guy. We shouldn't feel one way or the other about somebody we knew for two minutes. He's probably fine and well and good and dead and can't come back for revenge (provided you stay out of weird dimensional vortices in random weirdoes homes... which we'll probably be doing a lot of).
Still, free crystal!

20:10: This is both a shout-out to the _Friday the 13th_ slasher flick movies (with their usual setting being Camp Crystal Lake) and an even more direct reference to a bizarre easter egg you can unlock either at the midway point or the near-end of _West of Loathing_ ; specifically, to your protagonist of that game using an El Vibrato key to enter a Time Portal and wander a surreal wasteland where all the moments of time (the present, the past, the future) are crunched and melded together, including a forest near Camp Crystaldream Lake with a car containing a "newfangled six-shooter (a M1911A1 Handgun with it's more squarish, mass produced frame and a slide cartridge, as opposed to the guns of your time, old hand-loader, chambered revolvers or ball-loading flintlocks)" which could've protected a teenager from the Loathingverse's Jason equivalent. Oops. 
There's also a robot half-buried in the sand and a crumbling pyramid with an open sarcophagi containing an unliving jawbone that tries to tell you something. If the game goes where I think it does, if it's somehow capable of perusing your past game data to tell whether you got the gun or not from the "weird horseless carriage," then it could perhaps lead to an the mother of all callbacks, where your current protagonist runs into  and chats with your previous protagonist, a kind of passing of the torch if you will (maybe even a revelation that your past character is distantly related to your current character, almost like JoJo's Bizarre Adventure, with the heroes being related to each other somehow).

Also Mark, Mantel is a specific type of climb. It means to push down on a hold to bring your feet up to meet your hands on the same hold. So yeah if you’re climbing over something and your put your hands on the top, push (or pull) down with your hands to support your weight and bring your feet up to the area your hands are at, so that you can then stand up at that level, you are mantling. If you just pull yourself up with your hands and roll over at the top, or are just finding holds at different levels for your feet and hands to work your way up, you’re just climbing up. Typically, to reach another level of something, you are almost always going to be mantling at the very end of a climb. Wherever that last hold is, if your goal is to end up standing up at a higher elevation where you end up grabbing the ground where you will end up standing at at the top and do not have another hold above that to keep going, you will end up mantling at the end pretty much 100% of the time. However in situations like climbing a ladder, most of the time you don’t end up mantling at the end of the ladder is tall enough where the rungs continue above the level you’re trying to reach enough to where you can just step off at the end. 

Kinda pointless information I know, but also a kinda interesting random fact if you were ever curious. I only know this from a brief amount of time when I was a bit younger when I was into rock climbing. So yeah, typically in most video games you’re mostly mantling especially when all you’re doing is grabbing a ledge and pulling your legs up to get your feet onto the same ledge to stand up

I know that you record these in large sessions, but I figured I'd give some tips anyway.

Blocking attacks reduces the damage you take, but there is a way to completely negate the damage. If you initiate a block at the exact moment the attack would land, you perform a 'Perfect Block', which gives a 100% damage reduction to that attack, doesn't drain any stamina (meaning you can't get stunned), and may stun the enemy. Learn the attacks of the different enemies and practice your perfect blocks. Perfecting this skill will allow you to solo basically anything in the game, even wolf spiders. I would recommend using a Weevil Shield whilst learning, as this will negate all damage on a non-perfect block (this still drains stamina and can stun you).

Fiber Bandages heal a small amount instantly, and then heal a much larger amount over time. Get into the habit of using a single fiber bandage after most combats. There is a way to drastically reduce the crafting costs of fiber bandages, but I'll leave that to you guys to discover.

Spears give one of the highest dps of all weapons, but very little stun. In a group, I would recommend having one person use a heavy weapon, such as the spiky sprig or red ant club (which was unlocked this episode), while the others use pebblet spears. Focusing on one particular weapon type for combat gives advantages to the player using that weapon type, but I won't spoil any further.

Good luck in the Yard!
